findings.title: Offline publisher has no owner authentication
findings.proof: GET /api/publisher returned the synthetic private draft; PUT /api/publisher with no owner key replaced the publisher document and returned 200.
findings.impact: A process or another local account able to reach the loopback port can read unpublished content and modify the public content snapshot served by the launcher. This is not a demonstrated remote Internet exploit.
findings.fix: Require require_owner() for GET and PUT publisher. Update local company.js to send the owner key rather than exempting localhost. Retain origin/Host checks as additional controls.

findings.title: Offline briefs inbox exposes private enquiries without an owner key
findings.proof: An unauthenticated GET /api/briefs returned the synthetic private brief, including name, email, goal and budget fields.
findings.impact: Any caller able to access the loopback service can retrieve local commissioning enquiries. Normal remote websites are constrained by the existing origin/Host checks and browser same-origin policy.
findings.fix: Require owner authentication for the inbox; change the local UI to authenticate too. Test that public content remains readable while briefs and drafts do not.

findings.title: Submission throttling trusts request IP headers without a proxy boundary
findings.state: Local handler bypass confirmed; live exploitability unproven
findings.proof: Same socket and x-real-ip produced [201,201,201,201,201,429]. Changing x-real-ip produced seven further 201 responses against real disposable PostgreSQL.
findings.impact: A direct or incorrectly proxied deployment can evade application limits and generate spam or database costs. Vercel may replace these headers; that ingress behavior was not tested.
findings.fix: Define and verify the trusted hosting ingress, reject unsupported direct ingress, and use the hosting platform trusted client-address contract. Add a global submission budget and abuse controls so limits do not rely only on IP.

findings.title: Unauthenticated requests consume the valid owner request budget
findings.proof: 120 anonymous owner-endpoint requests consumed the shared owner-api/IP window. A subsequent request with the correct owner key received 429.
findings.impact: A caller sharing the owner’s egress IP can temporarily block the review/publishing desk; spoofable identity would expand the impact. No production flooding was performed.
findings.fix: Separate unauthenticated failure limits from authenticated owner traffic; retain a pre-auth abuse cap while applying a distinct authenticated principal budget.

findings.title: One long-lived owner key grants all administrative powers
findings.state: Design risk confirmed by source; no credential theft demonstrated
findings.proof: Owner authentication uses a single environment secret with no user identity, role split or expiry. The publisher retains it in sessionStorage.
findings.impact: A stolen key grants review, pricing, publishing and deletion powers. Individual staff cannot be revoked independently; a same-origin script compromise could read the publisher key.
findings.fix: Use named admin identities, MFA, role-limited authorization, expiring server sessions in secure HttpOnly cookies, revocation and an audit trail. Add CSRF protection when introducing cookie authentication. Keep applicant access keys separate.
findings.evidence: Source review; not an exploit receipt

findings.title: Offline static handler follows symlinks outside the public root
findings.proof: A symlink placed in the temporary served directory pointed to an outside marker file; GET returned that marker with 200.
findings.impact: If a public-root symlink points to private data, that target is readable through the launcher. This requires an existing symlink or filesystem write access; no traversal to arbitrary host files was demonstrated.
findings.fix: Resolve every static target and enforce containment within an explicit public root. Deny private filenames and directory listings; test the cross-platform asset path separately.

findings.title: Public responses have no Content Security Policy
findings.state: Confirmed by read-only public response headers
findings.proof: All three public origins returned no Content-Security-Policy header in sampled root and health responses. HSTS, nosniff and SAMEORIGIN were present.
findings.impact: There is less containment if an injection or compromised script is introduced. Missing CSP alone does not prove an XSS vulnerability.
findings.fix: Deploy a tested Report-Only policy first, then enforce a nonce/hash-based policy compatible with Three.js workers, shaders and assets. Include object-src, base-uri and frame-ancestors restrictions; do not break the current import map with an untested blanket policy.

findings.title: Lock Review Desk can be undone by an in-flight response
findings.state: Reproduced in local and live UI using intercepted synthetic responses
findings.proof: Unlock, start a second review fetch, click Lock Review Desk, then release the delayed response. Synthetic private application data reappears in the locked desk.
findings.impact: Data already requested by an authorized operator can be redrawn after they deliberately lock the screen. This is a privacy/session-state race, not a demonstrated bypass of the production backend owner key. All live test API requests were intercepted; no real credentials or records were used.
findings.fix: Increment an owner session epoch on lock, abort outstanding owner requests and reject stale responses before touching DOM. Clear pricing/private UI state, and require a new successful authentication before rendering it again.

findings.title: Empty existing offline owner key disables effective authentication
findings.state: Reproduced with a temporary empty key file
findings.proof: With an existing zero-byte commission-owner.key, startup proceeds and GET /api/applications without X-Lunar-Owner returns 200.
findings.impact: Requires an empty/whitespace owner-key file, for example after a failed initialization or manual edit. Normal freshly generated keys are not empty. The hosted API independently rejects short configured keys and is not implicated.
findings.fix: Validate minimum key strength on startup and again during authorization. Fail closed on invalid files and provide explicit repair/rotation instructions. Create/write the key atomically so interrupted initialization cannot leave a valid-looking empty file.
